headline: Ex-Cantonment Police chief placed on 5-day remand in sedition case
summary: Former Dhaka Cantonment OC Rakibul Hasan was arrested on Thursday for allegedly conspiring to undermine state stability and overthrow the government.
details: A Dhaka court has placed former Dhaka Cantonment Police chief Rakibul Hasan on a five-day remand following his arrest on Thursday afternoon.
The order was passed by Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Didarul Alam after hearing a petition filed by the investigating officer.
Rakibul is facing charges of sedition, with allegations that he conspired with unidentified accomplices to undermine state stability and overthrow the government.
The prosecution alleges that Rakibul harboured contempt and hatred toward high-ranking authorities, senior government officials, and security forces, using incitement to destabilise the country.
Defence lawyer Morshed Hossain Shahin opposed the remand, arguing that Rakibul is a dedicated government employee with no prior complaints against him.
The lawyer further claimed that the remarks for which he was arrested were exaggerated and that the arrest was a 'motivated and conspiratorial move' based on false allegations.
Despite the defense's plea for bail, the court granted the remand to facilitate further investigation into the evidence linking him to the incident.
caption:
A former Dhaka Cantonment Police chief has been placed on a 5-day remand for sedition.

A Dhaka court has placed former Dhaka Cantonment Police chief Rakibul Hasan on a five-day remand following his arrest on Thursday afternoon.

The order was passed by Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Didarul Alam after hearing a petition filed by the investigating officer.

Rakibul is facing charges of sedition, with allegations that he conspired with unidentified accomplices to undermine state stability and overthrow the government.

The prosecution alleges that Rakibul harboured contempt and hatred toward high-ranking authorities, senior government officials, and security forces, using incitement to destabilise the country.

Defence lawyer Morshed Hossain Shahin opposed the remand, arguing that Rakibul is a dedicated government employee with no prior complaints against him.

The lawyer further claimed that the remarks for which he was arrested were exaggerated and that the arrest was a 'motivated and conspiratorial move' based on false allegations.

Despite the defense's plea for bail, the court granted the remand to facilitate further investigation into the evidence linking him to the incident.

headline_marked: [[Banglalink gets nod for Starlink service]] in Bangladesh
headline: Banglalink gets nod for Starlink service in Bangladesh
summary: The BTRC has approved a limited Direct-to-Cell service, making Bangladesh the first South Asian country to introduce the technology.
details: Banglalink has received approval from the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) to launch a limited Starlink Direct-to-Cell service.
The service allows standard 4G LTE mobile phones to connect directly to Starlink satellites without needing special handsets, dishes, or custom apps.
Initially, subscribers with 4G-enabled handsets will be able to access SMS, data messaging, and WhatsApp calls in areas with Direct-to-Cell coverage.
The technology aims to extend connectivity to remote areas beyond conventional networks, including the sea, remote islands, coastal communities, and hill tracts.
It is expected to be particularly useful for fishermen, remote communities, and travelers in locations without mobile coverage.
The service could also serve as a critical communication alternative during cyclones, floods, and other natural disasters when mobile towers are damaged or unavailable.
Banglalink CEO Johan Buse stated that the goal is to ensure people in remote areas or during disasters do not have to worry about being beyond the reach of mobile services.
caption:
Bangladesh becomes the first South Asian country to introduce Starlink's Direct-to-Cell technology via Banglalink.

Banglalink has received approval from the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) to launch a limited Starlink Direct-to-Cell service.

The service allows standard 4G LTE mobile phones to connect directly to Starlink satellites without needing special handsets, dishes, or custom apps.

Initially, subscribers with 4G-enabled handsets will be able to access SMS, data messaging, and WhatsApp calls in areas with Direct-to-Cell coverage.

The technology aims to extend connectivity to remote areas beyond conventional networks, including the sea, remote islands, coastal communities, and hill tracts.

It is expected to be particularly useful for fishermen, remote communities, and travelers in locations without mobile coverage.

The service could also serve as a critical communication alternative during cyclones, floods, and other natural disasters when mobile towers are damaged or unavailable.

Banglalink CEO Johan Buse stated that the goal is to ensure people in remote areas or during disasters do not have to worry about being beyond the reach of mobile services.
